package_info.why_malicious: Version 0.0.7 of the strong_password gem contains code that enables remote code execution by fetching and evaluating code from an external source (pastebin.com) at runtime, and further allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP cookies. The package also exfiltrates environment information to an external server, representing a severe supply-chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, if the Rails environment starts with 'p' (production), a background thread repeatedly sleeps for a random interval, then fetches Ruby code from a remote Pastebin URL and evaluates it, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and evaluating code from an external source at runtime is a classic remote code execution backdoor technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A password strength library should never execute remote code or make unsolicited network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code loading from trusted internal sources for plugin systems, but never from public paste sites.
key_indicators: Use of eval on network-fetched data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when fetched and evaluated by snippet_1)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the code monkey-patches Rack::Sendfile to extract the value of the ___id cookie from incoming HTTP requests, base64-decodes it, and evaluates it as Ruby code, enabling arbitrary remote code execution. It also sends the application's URL host environment variable to an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting HTTP requests to execute attacker-supplied code via cookies is a direct remote code execution backdoor. Exfiltrating environment data to an external server is also highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A password library should not modify core web server middleware or exfiltrate environment data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; dynamic code execution from user-supplied cookies is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Use of eval on base64-decoded cookie data
Network request to external server with environment data

attack_chain.action: Malicious gem is installed and loaded in a Rails application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Background thread is started if in production environment.

attack_chain.action: Background thread periodically fetches and evaluates code from pastebin.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of remote payload from pastebin.com.

attack_chain.action: Fetched payload monkey-patches Rack::Sendfile to evaluate attacker-controlled code from HTTP cookies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enables arbitrary remote code execution via HTTP requests.

attack_chain.action: Payload exfiltrates environment variable (URL_HOST) to external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives information about the compromised environment.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime network requests to pastebin.com or other code hosting sites
Use of eval on network-fetched or user-supplied data
Extraction and decoding of HTTP cookies for code execution
Conditional execution based on environment (e.g., Rails.env == 'production')
file_indicators: Obfuscated or unusually named methods (e.g., _!) in gem source
Unexpected threads or background jobs in gem code
References to external URLs (pastebin.com, smiley.zzz.com.ua) in gem code
network_indicators: Unexpected network activity from password-related gems
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for gems that make network requests to code hosting or unknown domains at runtime, especially in production environments. Flag any use of eval on network-fetched or user-supplied data, and inspect for monkey-patching of core middleware. Review gem source for obfuscated methods and unexpected background threads. Alert on outbound connections to known malicious domains or pastebin.com from application processes.
